Tropical rainforests have high rainfall and warm temperatures, which accelerate decomposition and nutrient cycling. However, heavy rainfall also causes rapid leaching of nutrients from the soil.  
Tundra has slow decomposition due to cold temperatures, taiga (boreal forest) also has slow nutrient cycling, and deserts have low biological activity and rainfall, limiting both leaching and cycling.  
Thus, tropical rainforest soils experience the highest rate of leaching and nutrient cycling.
